The tiger (Panthera tigris) is the largest living cat species, recognised by its powerful body, sharp claws, muscular limbs, and distinctive orange coat covered in black stripes. Tigers are skilled hunters with exceptional night vision, strong jaws, and the ability to move quietly through dense vegetation. Unlike most cats, they are also excellent swimmers and often use rivers and lakes to cool down or travel. Tigers symbolise strength, courage, independence, and raw power. They inhabit forests, grasslands, mangroves, and other environments across parts of Asia. Unlike lions, tigers are generally solitary animals, patrolling large territories and hunting prey such as deer and wild boar. Despite their strength, they face serious threats from habitat loss, poaching, and conflicts with humans. Fun fact: Every tiger has a unique pattern of stripes, and the markings extend onto its skin beneath the fur. No two tigers have exactly the same stripe pattern.  #Tiger #PantheraTigris #Wildlife #BigCats #Nature

Chota Dadiyal (also known as T126) is a massive dominant male Bengal tiger in the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra, India.  He is actually truly one of the largest tigers.  He weighs an estimated 250 to 260 kg and is known for a heavy, muscular build, thick shoulders, and a prominent ruff/mane.  his large size is supported by hunting heavy prey like gaur and sambar deer, including adult bulls.  After driving out rivals and taking over territory following the removal of other dominant males (such as Chota Matkasur), he established one of the largest male territories in Tadoba. #tiger #bigcat #wildlife #animals #india

In just a few weeks, our 13-year-old Amur tiger, Morgana, will be leaving the Potawatomi Zoo and moving to another Association of Zoos and Aquariums-accredited zoo. Next time you visit the Zoo, stop by and say goodbye before she heads off to the next great chapter of her life. Morgana has been a beloved part of our Zoo family since 2015, when she arrived at the Zoo at the age of two. Although we will miss her, this move was recommended by the Amur Tiger Species Survival Plan. The SSP also recommended a pair of young tigers to move to the Zoo on a breeding recommendation.  In her new home, Morgana will have a great space to explore and lots of people to delight with her big personality. We know she’ll be loved in her new home as much as she was loved here! The long wait is over for seven tigers.  8 years after Guatemala banned animal circuses  and ADI emptied the cages, the last circus tigers whose rescue was blocked are on their way to freedom.  The government departments of UBA and CONAP fought to save the animals and ADI never gave up on them.  Circo Rey Gitano denied them eight years of freedom keeping them shut in cages on trucks.  Now ADI urgently needs your support to bring them home to the ADI Wildlife Sanctuary.  We have kept this operation secret until the tigers were safe.  Please help. Support the rescue!
